fractional-coo.title: Fractional COO: When and Why Your Business Needs One
fractional-coo.summary: Senior operational leadership on a flexible basis—when it fits, what to expect, and how it differs from generic consulting.
fractional-coo.p1: Growing businesses often hit a point where the founder or CEO is still the default operator—approving purchases, unblocking projects, and translating strategy for every team. A fractional COO brings senior operational leadership without the cost and commitment of a full-time executive hire.
fractional-coo.p2: Fractional COO engagements typically focus on priorities, owners, and KPIs; process improvements that reduce cycle time; and implementation support so recommendations become weekly habits—not binderware. Roalla applies this operator mindset inside Business Enablement programs and alongside digital builds when execution discipline matters.
fractional-coo.p3: You may be ready for fractional operational support if growth is outpacing your planning rhythm, handoffs between teams are breaking, or leadership needs board-ready clarity on the next 90 days. The fit is especially strong when you want someone in the room for decisions—not a report delivered afterward.

process-optimization.p1: Process optimization starts with observing how work actually moves—not how the org chart says it should. The highest-leverage fixes are usually handoffs: duplicate data entry, unclear ownership, and tools that don't talk to each other.
process-optimization.p2: Roalla's Transform phase builds inside review checkpoints—mapping workflows, removing manual steps, and connecting CRM, email, forms, and internal systems where integrations make sense. Clients often see reporting drop from hours to minutes once data flows automatically.

smb-digitization-benefits.metadataDescription: Why small and mid-size businesses invest in digitization—faster decisions, fewer errors, better customer experience, and a foundation for growth without enterprise budgets.
smb-digitization-benefits.title: Digitization for SMBs: Why It Matters Now
smb-digitization-benefits.summary: The practical benefits small and mid-size businesses gain from going digital—and what to prioritize first.
smb-digitization-benefits.p1: Small and mid-size businesses (SMBs) often delay digitization because it sounds expensive, disruptive, or reserved for larger competitors. In practice, the opposite is usually true: staying on spreadsheets, email threads, and disconnected tools creates hidden costs—slow quotes, missed follow-ups, duplicate data entry, and decisions made without current numbers.
smb-digitization-benefits.p2: Digitization for an SMB doesn't mean replacing everything at once. It means connecting the workflows that matter most: how you capture leads, schedule work, invoice customers, and report to leadership. Even modest improvements—a modern website with clear conversion paths, CRM connected to your inbox, or a custom portal for repeat clients—reduce friction your team feels every week.
smb-digitization-benefits.p3: The benefits compound quickly. Teams spend less time hunting for information. Customers get faster responses and a more professional experience. Owners gain visibility into pipeline, capacity, and cash flow without waiting for someone to rebuild a spreadsheet. That clarity is what lets an SMB grow without adding headcount at the same pace.
smb-digitization-benefits.p4: Roalla works with SMBs through Digital Enablement—scoped builds, integrations, and automation sized to your stage, not an enterprise playbook. Start with our five-question assessment or a service inquiry if you want help identifying the highest-return digitization move for your business.

smb-digital-efficiency.metadataDescription: How SMBs cut manual work and hidden costs through workflow automation, system integrations, and purpose-built digital tools.
smb-digital-efficiency.title: Digitization That Saves SMBs Time and Money
smb-digital-efficiency.summary: How connected systems, automation, and modern tools reduce manual work and hidden costs.
smb-digital-efficiency.p1: The biggest digitization payoff for SMBs often isn't a flashy app—it's eliminating work that shouldn't require a person. Re-keying form submissions into a CRM, copying numbers between spreadsheets for weekly reports, chasing status updates across email, and fixing errors caused by outdated files all consume hours that add up to real payroll cost.
smb-digital-efficiency.p2: Efficiency gains start with mapping where work stalls. Roalla's Transform phase identifies handoffs that can be automated or simplified: connecting your website forms to CRM, syncing scheduling tools with billing, or building lightweight dashboards that pull live data instead of manual exports. Clients often see reporting drop from hours to minutes once information flows automatically.
smb-digital-efficiency.p3: Not every bottleneck needs custom software. Sometimes the right fix is a better integration, clearer roles, or a focused internal tool when off-the-shelf products force awkward workarounds. The goal is the same: your team spends time on work that grows the business, not on moving data between systems.
smb-digital-efficiency.p4: If manual processes are eating your margin, Digital Enablement may be the fastest path to relief. Our assessment helps distinguish between a quick automation win, an integration project, and a custom platform—so you invest in the fix that matches your size and budget.

smb-digital-growth.metadataDescription: How SMBs use websites, platforms, and integrated workflows to win customers, respond faster, and scale without proportional headcount growth.
smb-digital-growth.title: How Digitization Helps SMBs Compete and Grow
smb-digital-growth.summary: Win more customers, respond faster, and scale operations without adding headcount.
smb-digital-growth.p1: SMBs compete on responsiveness, trust, and specialization—not on having the largest team. Digitization levels the field: a well-built website establishes credibility before the first call, online booking and self-service portals reduce back-and-forth, and integrated follow-up ensures no lead sits untouched because someone forgot to check a shared inbox.
smb-digital-growth.p2: Growth-stage SMBs hit a predictable ceiling when the founder or a small leadership team becomes the bottleneck for every quote, approval, and customer update. Digital systems absorb repeatable work—routing inquiries, tracking project status, sending reminders, and surfacing KPIs—so leadership can focus on decisions that require judgment, not data gathering.
smb-digital-growth.p3: The businesses that scale cleanly usually digitize in sequence: a conversion-focused web presence first, then systems that connect sales to delivery, then automation and custom tools where generic software falls short. Roalla's Prepare → Transform → Emerge → Soar model mirrors that path—align goals before you build, ship production-ready work, and iterate as volume increases.
smb-digital-growth.p4: Whether you're preparing for your next growth phase or trying to keep up with demand today, Roalla scopes digital work to SMB realities—clear milestones, accountable delivery, and tools your team will actually use. Submit a service inquiry or take the five-minute assessment to find your best starting point.

search-and-ai-visibility.metadataTitle: Search and AI Visibility: Why It Isn't One-Size-Fits-All | ROALLA
search-and-ai-visibility.metadataDescription: How to get found in web search and AI tools—why visibility strategy depends on your market, offering, and customers, and what separates attention from being lost in the crowd.
search-and-ai-visibility.title: Getting Found Online: Search, AI, and Why One Size Doesn't Fit All
search-and-ai-visibility.summary: Understanding how you appear in web search and AI tools can mean the difference between attention and being lost in the crowd—and the right approach depends on your business.
search-and-ai-visibility.p1: Your next customer may find you through Google, a map listing, a referral link—or by asking an AI assistant who serves businesses like theirs. Each channel works differently, and treating them as interchangeable is how good companies disappear. A local trades firm, a niche B2B consultant, and a regional SaaS vendor all need visibility, but none should copy the same playbook.
search-and-ai-visibility.p2: Traditional search still rewards clarity: pages that explain what you do in plain language, load quickly, work on mobile, and earn trust through useful content and credible structure. AI-driven discovery adds another layer—tools that summarize, recommend, and compare providers pull from how clearly your site describes your services, who you serve, and why you're credible. Vague copy, thin pages, and outdated information don't just hurt rankings; they make it harder for both search engines and AI systems to confidently recommend you.
search-and-ai-visibility.p3: There is no universal checklist. A business that wins on local intent needs strong location signals, reviews, and service-area clarity. A specialist competing nationally needs depth on the problems you solve—not generic blog filler. An SMB entering a crowded category needs differentiation baked into titles, headings, and proof points so humans and algorithms alike understand why you're the right fit. The common thread is specificity: the businesses that get attention say exactly who they help and how, in language their buyers actually use.
search-and-ai-visibility.p4: Roalla builds websites and digital presence with discovery in mind—structured content, conversion paths, and technical foundations sized to how your market actually searches. If you're investing in a new site or refresh and want to be found—not buried—start with a service inquiry or our five-minute assessment. We'll help you scope an approach that fits your business, not a template meant for everyone.

how-ai-systems-understand-websites.metadataTitle: How AI Systems Understand Business Websites | ROALLA
how-ai-systems-understand-websites.metadataDescription: Learn how clear entities, services, accessible HTML, structured information, public documentation, and trustworthy sources help AI systems interpret a business website.
how-ai-systems-understand-websites.title: How AI Systems Understand Business Websites
how-ai-systems-understand-websites.summary: AI systems do not experience your website like a customer. They assemble meaning from accessible text, structure, consistency, and corroborating public information.
how-ai-systems-understand-websites.p1: An AI assistant trying to describe your business looks for explicit facts: your organization name, services, audience, locations, expertise, policies, and proof. If those facts are scattered across decorative layouts, image-only sections, conflicting profiles, or vague marketing language, the system has to infer more—and may infer incorrectly.
how-ai-systems-understand-websites.p2: Clear HTML headings, descriptive links, accessible page structure, direct service explanations, and consistent organization information make those facts easier to extract. Structured data can reinforce relationships between the organization, its services, authors, locations, and content, but it cannot rescue a page whose visible information is thin or contradictory.
how-ai-systems-understand-websites.p3: Public documentation and specific use cases are especially valuable for digital products. A product page should explain who the product serves, what problem it solves, how it works, and where authoritative support information lives. Case studies, policies, contact details, and credible external references help establish trust around those claims.
how-ai-systems-understand-websites.p4: No site owner can force an AI platform to crawl, cite, or include a page in an answer. The practical goal is to publish accurate, accessible, well-structured information that people and machines can interpret consistently, then monitor how that information appears and correct gaps over time.

structured-data-for-small-business.metadataDescription: A practical guide to structured data for organizations, services, local businesses, articles, FAQs, products, and website navigation without unsupported claims.
structured-data-for-small-business.title: Structured Data for Small Businesses: What It Does and Where to Start
structured-data-for-small-business.summary: Structured data helps machines identify the meaning and relationships already visible on a page. It is useful infrastructure—not a shortcut to rankings or AI citations.
structured-data-for-small-business.p1: Structured data is machine-readable information added to a page, usually using Schema.org vocabulary in JSON-LD. It can identify an organization, service, product, article, breadcrumb trail, local business, or frequently asked question and connect that item to a canonical URL and publisher.
structured-data-for-small-business.p2: For most small businesses, the useful starting point is modest: Organization or LocalBusiness information, WebSite data, breadcrumbs, accurate Service data, and Article data for genuine editorial content. Product or SoftwareApplication data can help when a real product page contains the matching visible details.
structured-data-for-small-business.p3: The markup must agree with what visitors can see. Invented ratings, hidden FAQ answers, unsupported prices, or exaggerated service areas create risk rather than value. Validation tools can confirm syntax, but business owners still need to verify that names, URLs, contact details, and relationships are accurate.
structured-data-for-small-business.p4: Structured data does not guarantee a rich result, ranking, citation, or generated answer. Its value is clarity and consistency: it reduces ambiguity about what a page represents and gives search and answer systems a cleaner factual foundation to evaluate alongside content, accessibility, performance, and trust.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Find answers to common questions about our services and how we can help your business.
faq.stillHaveQuestions: Still have questions? We're here to help.
faq.a0: Fractional COO services provide businesses with senior-level operational expertise on a part-time or project basis. This allows companies to access strategic operational leadership without the cost of a full-time COO, making it ideal for growing businesses that need expert operational guidance.
faq.q1: How long does a typical Business Enablement engagement last?
faq.a1: Engagement duration varies based on your needs. Some projects are short-term (1-3 months) for specific initiatives, while others are ongoing partnerships. We work flexibly to match your business requirements and can adjust our involvement as your needs evolve.
faq.a2: We work with businesses across various industries including technology, manufacturing, professional services, retail, healthcare, and more. Our methodologies are adaptable to different business models and sectors.
faq.a3: We take confidentiality seriously. All team members sign non-disclosure agreements, and we follow strict data security protocols. Your business information is treated with the utmost discretion and protected at all times.
faq.q4: What happens after I submit a service inquiry?
faq.a4: We review your submission and respond within one business day with next steps—typically a brief discovery conversation to clarify scope, fit, and timing. There is no obligation to proceed.
faq.q5: Do you work with small businesses?
faq.a5: Absolutely! We work with businesses of all sizes, from startups to established companies. Our services are scalable and tailored to meet the specific needs and budgets of each client, regardless of company size.
faq.q6: How quickly can you start working with us?
faq.a6: We typically can begin engagements within 1-2 weeks of our initial conversation, depending on project scope and our current capacity. For urgent matters, we can often accommodate faster timelines.
faq.q7: What makes Roalla different from other advisory firms?
faq.a7: We combine strategy with accountable delivery—websites, apps, integrations, and automation built by the same team that guides the engagement. We don't just recommend; we ship production-ready work and stay through launch and iteration.
faq.a8: Digital enablement is the practical work of making your business run better online—websites, custom apps, integrations, workflow automation, and AI where it helps. Roalla guides each engagement from first scope through launch using our Prepare → Transform → Emerge → Soar model.
faq.q9: How much does a business website cost?
faq.a9: Focused business websites often land in a scoped range after a short discovery conversation—timeline and investment depend on pages, integrations, content readiness, and launch requirements. See our Website Design page for typical 1–4 week scopes, or submit a service inquiry for a tailored estimate.
faq.q10: How long does it take to build a custom web app or platform?
faq.a10: Small focused tools can ship in a few weeks; larger platforms with integrations, roles, and workflows typically run several sprints over one to three months. We align on milestones during Prepare so you know what ships when before full build investment.
faq.q11: Can you integrate our CRM, email, and existing tools?
faq.a11: Yes. Integrations and workflow automation are core Digital Enablement services—we connect CRMs, forms, email, calendars, payment tools, and internal systems so data flows without duplicate entry. See our Integrations & Automation section for examples.
faq.q12: What's the difference between digital enablement and digital transformation?
faq.a12: Digital transformation is often used as a broad label for organizational change. Digital enablement is what we deliver: concrete websites, apps, integrations, and automation that your team uses every week—with accountable delivery, not slide decks alone.
faq.q13: Can you add AI to our workflows?
faq.a13: We add practical AI where it helps—scoring, guided workflows, document automation, and API-backed assistants—not hype for its own sake. AI Support is part of our Digital Enablement service alongside integrations and custom platforms.
faq.q14: Do you work with startups and small businesses?
faq.a14: Yes. We work with owner-operated businesses, growth-stage teams, and larger enterprises. Scopes are tailored to your stage, budget, and timeline—from a conversion-focused marketing site to a custom platform your team runs daily.
faq.q15: What is Prepare → Transform → Emerge → Soar?
faq.a15: It's Roalla's delivery model for every digital engagement. Prepare aligns goals and scope; Transform is the build inside review checkpoints; Emerge is your market-facing launch; Soar covers iteration and scale after go-live. The same model appears on our service and portfolio pages.
faq.q16: Do you build websites for businesses in Ontario or Burlington?
faq.a16: Yes. Roalla is based in Burlington, Ontario, and serves clients across Canada and globally. Website design engagements include staging reviews, mobile-first builds, and launch support—whether you're local or remote.
faq.q17: Can you help with trade shows, booth kits, and event pages?
faq.a17: Yes. Our Digital Events service covers event landing pages, booth digital kits, QR paths, and apps ready when the floor opens. See our Digital Events page and portfolio examples like Boothlio and Cold Deja Bru.
faq.a18: We choose stacks based on your requirements—modern web frameworks, cloud hosting, APIs, and integration platforms that fit your team and budget. The priority is maintainable, production-ready systems your organization can run—not technology for its own sake.
faq.q19: How do workshops differ from Business Enablement programs?
faq.a19: Workshops are hands-on skill-building sessions—branding, sales, productivity, or ideation—for teams that want targeted learning. Business Enablement programs are broader advisory engagements covering strategy, operations, teams, data, and innovation with implementation support.

website-refresh.need: Our website looks outdated, or we don't have one yet.
website-refresh.consider: DIY builders (Wix, Squarespace, WordPress themes) are quick to start, but custom domains, mobile layouts, SEO, and forms often need extra plugins. Small changes can break layouts without someone who knows what changed—and you still own the content updates.
website-refresh.deliver: Conversion-focused sites with a clear next step—book, contact, or request a quote. Scoped to your timeline with one accountable team from brief through launch. See Kaylan Kaptures and Ryan Munce Goaltending for live brand-site examples.

lead-capture.need: We need more leads, bookings, or quote requests from our site.
lead-capture.consider: A contact form alone rarely converts. DIY setups often miss follow-up routing, spam protection, CRM handoff, and mobile-friendly flows. Leads sit in an inbox instead of reaching the right person.
lead-capture.deliver: Short, mobile-first forms tied to your CRM, inbox, or spreadsheet—with instant confirmations and the right person notified. GRC Status shows this pattern with assessment and preview CTAs on a compliance-focused site.

custom-app.need: We need a tool that fits our workflow—not a generic app.
custom-app.consider: Spreadsheets and no-code tools work until permissions, approvals, or integrations get complex. DIY often creates shadow IT: one person's clever setup that nobody else can maintain.
custom-app.deliver: Digital products and internal tools built around the value your business needs to create—revenue, customer self-service, or operational capability. Explore 8 verified digital product examples in our current portfolio.

client-portal.need: Clients or partners need a secure place to see status, files, or updates.
client-portal.consider: Sharing by email and shared drives gets messy fast—wrong versions, no audit trail, and login sprawl across tools. DIY portals from template marketplaces rarely match your branding or data rules.
client-portal.deliver: Branded portals with the access rules you need—status dashboards, document exchange, or guided steps. Built to your security and hosting preferences.

integrations.need: Our CRM, email, forms, and other tools don't share data cleanly.
integrations.consider: Zapier and native connectors help for simple paths, but edge cases—duplicate records, failed webhooks, field mismatches—pile up without monitoring. DIY integrations become fragile when any tool updates.
integrations.deliver: Reliable connections between the tools you already pay for—CRM, email, forms, sheets, and internal systems—with error handling and a clear owner when something changes.

workflow-automation.need: My team wastes time on repetitive copy-paste and manual handoffs.
workflow-automation.consider: Macros and DIY automation save minutes until an exception breaks the chain. Without documentation, only one person knows how it works—and they're on vacation when it fails.
workflow-automation.deliver: Documented automations for the handoffs that actually slow you down—onboarding, reporting, approvals, notifications—with a human-readable map of what runs when.

event-kit.need: We're exhibiting at a trade show or running a launch event.
event-kit.consider: Printing QR codes on flyers is easy; tracking which booth moment drove interest is not. DIY event pages often lack floor-friendly lead capture, offline contingencies, and post-show follow-up routing.
event-kit.deliver: Event pages, booth QR/NFC entry paths, floor-optimized lead capture, and post-show exports—ready when the floor opens. Built from our Digital Events playbook; Boothlio is a live product example.

ai-workflows.need: We want AI to help—not another chatbot nobody uses.
ai-workflows.consider: Generic AI plugins add novelty without measurable outcomes. DIY prompts drift, lack guardrails, and rarely connect to your CRM or documents. Teams hesitate without clear human review steps.
ai-workflows.deliver: Scoped AI inside real workflows—scoring, guided briefs, document assistance, and intelligent routing—with guardrails and human review. Live today in Pitch Hotshots.

privacy.intro:
This Privacy Policy explains how Roalla Business Enablement Group (“Roalla,” “we,” “us,” or “our”) collects, uses, discloses, retains, and protects personal information in connection with www.roalla.com and related business operations.

We are a Canadian organization based in Burlington, Ontario. We design our practices to align with the Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA) and applicable provincial privacy laws, and with Canada’s Anti-Spam Legislation (CASL) for commercial electronic messages. If you are in Québec, we also respect applicable requirements under Québec privacy legislation (including Law 25) to the extent they apply to our activities.
privacy.s1Body:
This Policy applies to personal information collected through our website, forms, email, phone, assessments, and related marketing or sales communications. It does not apply to third-party websites we link to, or to Roalla products that publish their own privacy notices (those notices control for those products).

Roalla is accountable for personal information under its control. Day-to-day privacy questions and requests: sales@roalla.com · (289) 838-5868 · Burlington, ON, Canada. You may ask for our privacy contact or designate when making a formal request.
privacy.s2Body:
Information you provide may include: name; email address; phone number; organization and role; project goals and requirements; assessment answers; industry and timeline preferences; URLs you share; message content; and other details you choose to submit.

Information collected automatically may include: IP address; approximate location derived from IP; browser and device type; operating system; pages viewed; referring/exit pages; date and time stamps; and diagnostic or security logs.

We do not knowingly seek sensitive personal information (such as health information, government identifiers, or biometric data) through the public website. Do not submit such information via public forms. If an engagement requires handling regulated data, that will be scoped under a written agreement with appropriate safeguards.
privacy.s3Title: 3. Purposes of collection and use (PIPEDA fair information principles)

Where CASL requires express or implied consent for commercial electronic messages, we obtain and honour that consent and provide an unsubscribe mechanism in marketing messages.

aiPolicy.title: AI Policy
aiPolicy.intro:
This AI Policy describes how Roalla Business Enablement Group (“Roalla,” “we,” “us”) uses artificial intelligence and automated systems in our website experiences, Digital Enablement work, Programs, and internal operations. It complements our Terms & Conditions and Privacy Policy.

We follow practical Canadian expectations for responsible AI: transparency, human accountability, privacy protection, security, and avoidance of prohibited harmful uses—consistent with guidance from Canadian public institutions and evolving federal frameworks.
aiPolicy.s1Body:
We use AI to improve quality and speed of research, drafting, summarization, scoring, triage, automation, testing support, and certain product features—where it creates clear business value.

Our principles: (1) AI assists; humans remain accountable for client-facing decisions and deliverables we stand behind; (2) privacy and confidentiality come first; (3) we aim for transparency when AI materially affects outcomes; (4) we design for security and misuse prevention; (5) AI is not a substitute for licensed professional advice (legal, tax, audit, medical, or regulated compliance advice).
aiPolicy.s2Body:
Examples include: assisting internal drafting and research; summarizing inquiry or workshop inputs; scoring or feedback features in Roalla products; generating draft copy or code that staff review; and automating routine operational tasks.

Marketing pages describe capabilities at a high level. The specific AI tools and workflows used on your project are confirmed during scoping or in the statement of work.
aiPolicy.s3Body:
Material client-facing outputs (proposals, production content, application logic, and recommendations we deliver under an engagement) are reviewed by Roalla personnel before delivery, unless a written agreement expressly describes automated or self-serve AI features.

You are responsible for reviewing AI-assisted outputs against your business, brand, regulatory, accessibility, and factual requirements before relying on them or publishing them. Critical decisions should not be based solely on automated AI output.
aiPolicy.s4Body:
We do not knowingly use confidential client materials to train public or general-purpose third-party AI models. Use of third-party AI providers is subject to our Privacy Policy, vendor agreements, and engagement confidentiality terms.

Where a workflow requires sending data to an AI provider, we will describe that use in the relevant product notice, proposal, or agreement. You must not submit personal information of others, regulated data, or secrets into public demo tools unless the engagement expressly authorizes that processing and safeguards are in place.
aiPolicy.s5Body:
AI systems can produce incomplete, outdated, biased, or incorrect results, and may “hallucinate” content. We use review checkpoints, grounding in your source materials, testing, and acceptance criteria to reduce risk, but we do not guarantee that AI outputs are error-free, complete, or fit for every purpose.

To the extent permitted by law, disclaimers and liability limits in our Terms and engagement agreements apply to AI-assisted work product and website features.
aiPolicy.s6Body:
Ownership of deliverables created under a paid engagement—including AI-assisted portions—is governed by the engagement agreement. Roalla does not claim ownership of your pre-existing materials.

You are responsible for ensuring that prompts and source materials you provide do not infringe third-party rights. Open-source or third-party model licences may impose additional conditions on generated outputs; we will flag material constraints we are aware of during scoping when relevant.
aiPolicy.s7Body:
You must not use Roalla AI features or request that we use AI to: violate law; create deceptive deepfakes or impersonations intended to harm; generate malware or cyberattack tooling; produce child sexual exploitation material or other illegal content; engage in unlawful discrimination; or circumvent security or rate limits.

We may refuse work or disable features that we reasonably believe involve prohibited or unacceptably high-risk uses, including uses that would require specialized regulated oversight we have not contracted to provide.
aiPolicy.s8Body:
When AI materially shapes a deliverable or customer-facing product feature, we aim to disclose that in demos, documentation, statements of work, or in-product notices so you can make informed decisions.

If you need documentation for your own compliance program (for example vendor questionnaires), request it during discovery and we will provide reasonably available information about our AI practices for that engagement.
aiPolicy.s9Body:
We apply access controls and vendor due diligence appropriate to the sensitivity of data processed with AI tools. Suspected misuse, leakage, or security incidents involving AI systems should be reported promptly to sales@roalla.com.

Privacy incidents are handled under our Privacy Policy and applicable Canadian law.
